question: How many politicians will leave their cabinet positions in the UK government before 2027?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no departures among the 18 listed Burnham cabinet members found as of 30 Sep 2026 (~25% of the Sep1-Dec31 window elapsed). Reference class: newly formed UK cabinets in their first ~5 months rarely lose top-18 members (Starmer: Haigh at ~4 months; May 2016/Johnson 2019: none; Truss 2022: crisis outlier). Remaining ~3 months implies ~25% chance of >=1 departure. Upward risks: Healey's first Budget 28 Oct amid 95% debt/GDP and high gilt yields; volatile Labour year; ministers with past scandal baggage (Rayner resigned Sep 2025). Downward: fresh cabinet makes a reshuffle unlikely. Markets: Polymarket 'first to leave Burnham cabinet' contracts (close 2028) price individuals low (Healey 0.14, Fahnbulleh 0.10, Eagle 0.07); these don't match this question's terms and serve as evidence only, not an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Burnham ministry formed 20 Jul 2026 after Starmer resigned (announced 22 Jun) following May 2026 local-election losses and a leadership crisis; 15 Starmer-era cabinet members dismissed, the most in a same-party transition since Johnson 2019 (Wikipedia Burnham ministry, as of 30 Sep 2026).
- Wikipedia Burnham ministry and Premiership of Andy Burnham pages (both edited around 30 Sep 2026) show no cabinet changes after 20-23 Jul 2026. Searches for Sept 2026 cabinet resignations found nothing.
- Polymarket runs a 'first to leave the Burnham cabinet' series (created about 3 Aug 2026, closes 2028), which implies nobody had left at creation. Prices sit in the harness's market list; the contract is a near-miss (different deadline).
- Chancellor Healey's first Budget is set for 28 Oct 2026: debt about 95% of GDP, borrowing costs at multi-decade highs linked to the US-Iran war, and a tax-rise-plus-cuts package expected (Irish Times 28 Sep 2026; Bloomberg 27 Sep 2026).
- Labour conference was held late Sep 2026. No reports found of a minister under pressure to resign.
- Burnham visited Ukraine and the US; Trump praised him (about 22 Sep 2026).
- Historical reference points: Starmer cabinet lost Louise Haigh (Nov 2024, about 4 months in) and Angela Rayner (Sep 2025, followed by a reshuffle). May 2016 and Johnson Dec 2019 cabinets had no top-cabinet departures in their first 4-5 months. Truss 2022 lost Kwarteng and Braverman within about 6 weeks (crisis outlier). Sunak lost Williamson (Nov 2022, not a top-18 post) and Zahawi (Jan 2023, about 3 months in).
- Returning ministers with past controversies include Rayner (resigned Sep 2025 over stamp duty) and Streeting (resigned May 2026 to challenge Starmer).
- Resolution: counts any departure (sacking, resignation, reshuffle move out of the post, death) of the 18 named incumbents between 1 Sep and 31 Dec 2026, per the parliament.uk cabinet page (the page returned 403 when fetched). If the PM changes, the count freezes on that date.
- Event window: 2026-09-01 -> 2026-12-31 per the criteria; as of 2026-09-30, about 25% has elapsed with no qualifying departure found.
- Searched but not found: any September 2026 ministerial scandal, reshuffle plans, or bookmaker odds on the next cabinet exit.
calls.reference_class: UK cabinets in the first 2-5 months after a new PM forms a government (2016-2024), top-~18 member departures per 3-4 month window

calls.reasoning: No departures from the 18 listed posts since 1 Sep 2026 per Wikipedia (Burnham ministry, Premiership) and news up to 29 Sep (Rayner still active). Roughly 3 months remain. Reference class: in about a third of recent new UK governments (Truss yes, Starmer 2024 yes via Haigh, May 2016 no, Brown no, Sunak top-18 no), a top-18 cabinet member left in the equivalent window, recalled from memory rather than a sourced dataset. A fresh, loyal cabinet with a strong mandate and a quiet September pull slightly below that. Multiple departures without a reshuffle or crisis are rare. The PM-change clause freezes the count. Polymarket only has 'first to leave the Burnham cabinet' markets (Healey 0.14, Fahnbulleh 0.10, Eagle 0.07, Bryant 0.06, Mahmood 0.04, McFadden 0.03, by 2028). They are a near miss on both timing and count, so I did not use them as an anchor. No market matches this question's count/deadline.

Starmer 2024: Haigh resigned 29 Nov, month ~5 (yes). Johnson 2019: Rudd resigned Sep, month ~1.5 (borderline/early). Sunak 2022: Williamson Nov, not a top-18 post (no). May 2016: none until Nov 2017 (no). Brown 2007: Hain Jan 2008, month 7 (no). Cameron 2010: Laws in week 3 (early). Over these cases, roughly a third had a departure in a comparable ~3-month window. - Resolves off the parliament.uk cabinet page (403 when fetched) and the Metaculus fine-print list of 18 incumbents. A change of PM freezes the count at that date. The question counts people who leave their positions, so a reshuffle moving a person to a different post plausibly counts.

- Human markets: none found on the count of departures. Only Polymarket 'first to leave the Burnham cabinet' markets exist (different contract: who leaves first, by 2028).

calls.reasoning: Window 2026-09-01 to 2027-01-01, ~25% elapsed with no departures found among the 18 listed ministers (Wikipedia Burnham ministry, news through Labour conference late Sept). Cabinet only ~2 months old after a large July purge, so a reshuffle is unlikely; main risks are idiosyncratic scandal/resignation and the 28 Oct budget stress on Chancellor Healey. Historical Sep-Dec windows for UK cabinets: ~half have zero departures of senior cabinet; multi-departure windows are mostly reshuffles or crises. Remaining ~3 months implies Poisson-ish λ≈0.4-0.5 with cascade risk (a replacement may move another listed minister). Polymarket 'first to leave Burnham cabinet' (~$124k vol, Healey 14%, Fahnbulleh ~10%) resolves by end-2027, so is not an anchor for count by end-2026. No Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker market on the count found.

calls.reference_class: UK cabinet top-18 departures during Sep-Dec windows 2016-2025, weighted toward windows early in a PM's tenure

calls.reasoning: No departures among the 18 listed Burnham cabinet members as of 30 Sep 2026; ~3 months of the window remain for a ~10-week-old cabinet formed after a large purge, so an autumn reshuffle is unlikely. Reference class of new UK governments' months ~2-5 gives roughly 25-30% chance of at least one top-18 exit in a 3-month span; main idiosyncratic risks are Healey's 28 Oct Budget under fiscal stress and scandal baggage (e.g., Rayner). Conditional on one exit, cascades (a cabinet member moved to fill the gap, mini-reshuffle) make 2+ materially likely, fattening the tail. Polymarket 'first to leave the Burnham cabinet' (by 2028) is a near-miss contract, used as weak evidence only; no count/deadline-matching market found.
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the facts: 0 departures from 1-30 Sep 2026, ~75% of window remaining, no scandal or reshuffle talk found, Budget 28 Oct. Disputes were judgment: Runs 1-2 used a new-government reference class (~1/3 with an exit in a comparable window), while Run 3 used calendar Sep-Dec windows that include reshuffle years. I favour the new-government class because a reshuffle is improbable this soon after formation, but I side with Run 3 on cascade risk: 'leave their positions' plausibly counts a reshuffle move, and single exits often trigger a second move (e.g., Rayner 2025). So P(0) sits near Runs 1-2, with slightly fatter 2 and 3+ buckets. The one factual item, the Polymarket series' volume ($124k vs ~$5-24k per contract), can't be settled without web access and doesn't affect the estimate because the contract is a near-miss. Reference-class lists in the runs were from memory, so the base rate carries real uncertainty.
